title: Give the AI the failing test first
tip: Paste or point the assistant at a failing test before asking for a fix. A concrete pass/fail target beats a paragraph of description and stops it from 'fixing' the wrong thing.

title: Ask for a plan before code
tip: For anything bigger than one file, ask the AI to outline the files it will touch and why. Correcting a five-line plan is far cheaper than reviewing 300 lines of the wrong approach.

title: Keep a CLAUDE.md or rules file
tip: Write your project's conventions (package manager, test command, folder layout, do-nots) in a rules file the assistant reads every session. You stop repeating yourself and get consistent output.

title: Make the AI verify its own work
tip: End requests with 'run the type checker and tests, and show me the output'. Assistants that can run commands catch most of their own mistakes when you ask them to.

title: Small diffs, frequent commits
tip: Commit before every AI-driven change. If the result goes sideways, git restore is instant and you can retry with a better prompt instead of untangling a mess.

title: Feed it real examples
tip: Instead of describing your component style, point the AI at one existing component and say 'match this'. Examples transfer conventions better than rules.

title: Use AI to read, not just write
tip: Ask 'explain how data flows from this API route to this page' in an unfamiliar codebase. It's one of the highest-value, lowest-risk uses of an assistant.

title: Review AI code like a stranger's PR
tip: Check error handling, edge cases and anything touching auth or money line by line. AI code is fluent, which makes subtle bugs easier to miss.

title: Let AI write the boring tests
tip: Ask for table-driven tests covering edge cases (empty, null, unicode, huge input) for a pure function. Then delete the ones that test nothing meaningful.

title: Paste the whole error
tip: Give the full stack trace and the command you ran, not a summary. The file path and line in the trace are usually what the model needs most.

title: Default to Server Components
tip: In the App Router, components are server components unless you add 'use client'. Push 'use client' down to the smallest interactive leaf so less JavaScript ships to the browser.

title: Fetch in parallel
tip: In a server component, start independent requests together with Promise.all instead of awaiting one after another. Sequential awaits are a common cause of slow pages.

title: Stream slow parts with Suspense
tip: Wrap a slow section in <Suspense fallback={...}> so the rest of the page renders immediately. A loading.tsx file does this for a whole route segment.

title: Use next/image sizes
tip: Always set the sizes prop on responsive next/image elements. Without it the browser may download a much larger image than it displays.

title: Server Actions for simple mutations
tip: For form submits that just write data, a Server Action removes the need for a separate API route and works even before JavaScript loads.

title: Know your caching
tip: Check whether a fetch or route is cached before debugging 'stale data'. Read the caching docs for your Next.js version, since defaults changed between major versions.

title: next/font removes layout shift
tip: Load fonts with next/font. It self-hosts them and sets size-adjust fallbacks so text doesn't jump when the web font arrives.

title: generateMetadata for SEO
tip: Export generateMetadata from dynamic pages to build titles and Open Graph tags from the same data the page fetches. Requests are deduplicated.

title: Derive, don't sync, state
tip: If a value can be computed from props or other state during render, compute it. Copying it into useState with a useEffect to keep it in sync is a bug factory.

title: Keys reset components
tip: Changing a component's key remounts it with fresh state. It's the cleanest way to reset a form when the selected item changes.

title: You might not need an effect
tip: Effects are for syncing with external systems. Handling a click, transforming data, or reacting to a prop change usually belongs in an event handler or render.

title: useTransition for heavy updates
tip: Wrap a non-urgent state update (like filtering a big list) in startTransition so typing stays responsive while React renders the result.

title: Container queries
tip: Use @container to style a card by its own width, not the viewport's. Components then adapt wherever you drop them in a layout.

title: :has() is a parent selector
tip: form:has(input:invalid) or .card:has(img) lets you style a parent based on its children, with no JavaScript class toggling.

title: clamp() for fluid type
tip: font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem) scales smoothly between a minimum and maximum without breakpoints.

title: Use logical properties
tip: margin-inline and padding-block instead of left/right/top/bottom make layouts work automatically in right-to-left languages.

title: aspect-ratio prevents jumps
tip: Set aspect-ratio on media containers so space is reserved before images or embeds load, which improves your CLS score.

title: satisfies keeps literal types
tip: const config = {...} satisfies Config checks the shape but keeps the narrow literal types, so you get both validation and precise autocomplete.

title: Discriminated unions for state
tip: Model state as { status: 'loading' } | { status: 'error', error } | { status: 'ok', data }. Impossible states become unrepresentable.

title: Validate at the boundary
tip: Types vanish at runtime. Parse API responses and form data with a schema library such as Zod, then trust the types inside your app.

title: Exhaustive switch checks
tip: In a switch's default branch assign the value to a variable of type never. Adding a new union member then becomes a compile error until you handle it.

title: structuredClone for deep copies
tip: structuredClone(obj) deep-copies objects, including Dates, Maps and Sets. Skip JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) and its lost types.

title: AbortController for fetch
tip: Pass an AbortController signal to fetch and abort it when a component unmounts or a newer search starts, which avoids race conditions.

title: Array.prototype.at
tip: arr.at(-1) gets the last element. Cleaner than arr[arr.length - 1].

title: Object.groupBy
tip: Object.groupBy(items, i => i.category) groups an array in one line. It's supported in modern browsers and Node 21+.

title: Measure INP, not just load
tip: Interaction to Next Paint is a Core Web Vital. Use the Performance panel to find long tasks after clicks and split them up, or defer the work.

title: Preload the LCP image
tip: Find your Largest Contentful Paint element in Lighthouse. If it's an image, give it priority loading (fetchpriority=high, or priority on next/image).

title: Check your bundle
tip: Run a bundle analyzer once a month. One accidentally client-side date or chart library can add hundreds of kilobytes.

title: Buttons are buttons
tip: Use <button> for actions and <a> for navigation. A div with onClick misses keyboard support, focus and screen-reader semantics.

title: Test with only a keyboard
tip: Tab through your page once a week. If you can't see where focus is, or can't reach something, neither can many of your users.

title: Content Fragments + GraphQL for headless
tip: Model structured content as Content Fragment Models and query them with AEM's GraphQL API. Use persisted queries so responses are cacheable at the CDN.

title: Persisted queries over ad-hoc ones
tip: Persisted GraphQL queries are fetched with GET and cached by Dispatcher and the CDN. Ad-hoc POST queries bypass that cache and hit publish every time.

title: Universal Editor instrumentation
tip: The Universal Editor finds editable content through data-aue-* attributes in your markup. Instrument your Next.js components once and authors can edit in context.

title: Edge Delivery Services blocks
tip: In EDS, each block is a folder with block.js and block.css. Keep blocks small and decorate the authored table markup rather than fighting it.

title: Use the AEM headless SDK
tip: @adobe/aem-headless-client-js handles auth and persisted-query calls for you, which beats hand-rolling fetch wrappers around the GraphQL endpoint.

title: Schemas first in Experience Platform
tip: In AEP, design XDM schemas and field groups before ingesting data. Changing a schema after profiles are enabled is far more painful.

title: git switch -
tip: Like cd -, git switch - jumps back to the previous branch. Handy when bouncing between a feature branch and main.

title: Rebase with autosquash
tip: Commit fixes with git commit --fixup <sha>, then git rebase -i --autosquash main folds them into the right commits automatically.

title: git bisect finds regressions
tip: git bisect start, mark a good and a bad commit, and Git binary-searches the history. Add 'git bisect run npm test' to automate it.

title: Copy as fetch
tip: In the Network panel, right-click a request and choose Copy as fetch (or cURL) to replay an API call exactly, headers and all.

title: Local overrides
tip: Chrome DevTools > Sources > Overrides lets you edit a production file or response locally and reload, which is great for testing a fix before deploying.

title: Write it down
tip: Keep a weekly 'brag doc' of what you shipped and learned. It makes reviews, résumés and interviews dramatically easier.

title: Read one PR you didn't write
tip: Review or read one PR outside your area each day. It's the cheapest way to learn the rest of the codebase and other people's patterns.
